newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Yorks Water to cut holders' funds.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Yorks Water to cut holders' funds.

text.p: British regional utility Yorkshire Water Plc said on Friday it aimed to reduce shareholders' funds by the end of its financial year to help reduce its overall cost of capital.
"For an utility, we have relatively too much equity, and I think that's well recognised," chairman Brandon Gough told Reuters in an interview.
"We would like to have this dealt with by the end of the financial year," he added, noting that the company had yet to make a decision on how it would cut shareholders' funds.

"Until the Chancellor (of the Exchequer) threw a spanner in the works in October, probably the most logical route for a company like us would be a share buyback," Gough said, referring to recent UK tax changes that have made buyback programmes less attractive for companies.
He said Yorkshire currently has shareholder approval to buy back 10 percent of its shares, which would amount to some 140 million stg based on its existing market capitalisation.
"We're not promising that amount, but that is indicative of the scale of the adjustment we would make," he said.
